pr_title: Fix parsing SSL ACL along with others
pr_body:
##### Summary
It was reported to us that Netdata was not parsing properly the SSL acl sometimes. This PR fix this parsing the SSL acl before the common ACLs and avoiding netdata to took the wrong ACLs, because it could not be parsed correctly. 
##### Component Name
Socket.
##### Additional Information
Fixes  #6457 , #6471
pr_comments: I will generate a shell script that changes netdata.conf with different combinations for us to confirm that everything is ok, I changed manually some combinations in my own netdata.conf before to release this PR.
I brought some tests using a shell script file, this shell script does not support stream and SSL tests.

The failure on Travis stops due to shellchecking errors.
Try to install shellcheck and run it through all bash scripts you introduced to eliminate the warnings.

If there is a very peculiar warning that can't be fixed for a legitimate reason, you can disable it like so to make shellecheck stop shouting: `# shellcheck disable=SC2181` (where SC2181 is the error shellcheck spotted)

Hi everybody,

@paulkatsoulakis I used the shellcheck and I could fix a lot of warnings, but I cannot change the "chown" line as it was asked, because the chown gives me error and does not change the permission.

@cakrit I changed the things as you requested, but you will see that I am working with 3 different configuration files and the motive I was conducted to do this are bellow:

- The first test is the simplest possible with all ACLs, because I wanna be sure that everything is working properly with the default ACLs.
- The second test follows your requirement, and I am using ^SSL=optional, the results demonstrated that everything happened as expected.
- The third and last test forces the SSL and here again the results were according expected. When I was developing this test, I stopped it to verify that we were not missing ports during the redirect, that was the problem reported in the issue #6471,  I confirmed that all "Location" had address and port, so I think it was fixed.

Finally another thing that I remebered with the tests is the fact that the SSL when activated, it won't be activated for a specific port when we open more than one port, it will be active for the whole system. Case we decided to do it for specific ports, I suggest another PR to bring these changes, because it will need change in more files.

In the last two hours I tested everything and it looks like that the last commit is bringing what we were missing, but it is too late, so tomorrow morning I will read again the user requests and I will do another test to be sure I am not missing nothing.

@cakrit I sent message for our users and I retest everything with the script present in this PR and a VM to test the communication between master and slave, about this last, I could not find a simple way to have a shell script for everyone to test the communication, so I only tested with VM.

Unless somebody finds an error, I consider this finished.

[![CLA assistant check](https://cla-assistant.io/pull/badge/signed)](https://cla-assistant.io/netdata/netdata?pullRequest=6468)
All committers have signed the CLA.

About the global variable that was present in the master, it is not more present, I also saw that the variable is necessary only for the stream when it is a slave, so I moved it from the security.c to the rrdpush.c where it will be necessary to have it to read information from stream.conf and apply when connect with the master.
I ran tests with the script that is in this PR, I also tested with the browser and finally I tested the stream, I could not identify any error, it redirects when it was necessary, it did not send stream when the master was set as ^SSL=force and the slave did not use SSL, finally the stream could send encrypted information for both case(SSL either 'optional' or 'force').

Hi @cakrit ,

I fixed the problem with the default rule when the user does not set the SSL acl, considering that our team always advocate for readable code, I decided to use among the options available to fix this, the creation of a default FLAG that is set when nothing is giving to the port. 
It was also necessary to change the argument of the script, because the default behavior redirects more time than the previous version that had a bug.
All my tests passed now. There's only a mistake I made in the README, please make the correction and let's finally merge this one.

review_comments:
Do NOT use global variables for these. Look at socket.c L433 on how to apply ACL on each socket properly. 
We should have caught this from the first PR, it's not correct.

The Netdata does not have more global variable for incoming connections, I am only using global variable now for the SSL stream client, because we do not have the webclient structure in the stream initialization, we would need to create an analogous variable inside RRDHOST, but I did not find this necessary.

Did we have this before and verified it's not a problem? I don't remember...
![Screenshot from 2019-07-18 18-37-58](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43294513/61475589-73ceed00-a98b-11e9-9b45-2ea981cede58.png)
Yes it is a false positive, case you use an "alt+f7" inside clion, you will see that the function security_start_ssl is always called with a valid value.

This is completely wrong. You're not getting the entire config line here. In fact, the addition of `^SSL=whatever` will cause the last item in the `...=A|B|C^SSS=whatever` list of A,B,C to not match, because the parsing was not modified to only send A, B and C to `read_acl`. I will explain more in person.
